questions.question_es:
¿Qué imprime este código?

```python
class A(Exception): pass
class B(A): pass

try:
    raise A()
except B:
    print("B")
except A:
    print("A")
```
questions.question_en:
What does this code print?

```python
class A(Exception): pass
class B(A): pass

try:
    raise A()
except B:
    print("B")
except A:
    print("A")
```
options_es: Imprime B, porque B está primero y except elige la primera cláusula sin comprobar tipos.
Imprime A, porque except B no atrapa instancias de la clase base A.
Imprime B y luego A, porque ambas cláusulas se ejecutan en orden.
No imprime nada; la excepción A queda sin manejar y el programa termina con error.
options_en: It prints B, because B is listed first and except picks the first clause without checking types.
It prints A, because except B does not catch instances of the base class A.
It prints B and then A, because both clauses run in order.
It prints nothing; A stays unhandled and the program ends with an error.
questions.explanation_es: Una cláusula except atrapa instancias de la clase nombrada o de sus subclases, pero no al revés. Como se lanza A, que es la clase base de B, except B no coincide y se pasa a except A, que sí coincide y se ejecuta. Además, como mucho se ejecuta un manejador, así que no salen ambos mensajes.
questions.explanation_en: An except clause catches instances of the named class or of its subclasses, but not the other way around. Since A, the base class of B, is raised, except B does not match and Python moves on to except A, which does match and runs. Also, at most one handler runs, so both messages cannot appear.
questions.source: Python documentation — 8. Errors and Exceptions (https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html) — PSF-2.0
